converter_choice.19 V buck-boost: 19 V, >= 5 A (95-100 W), input 16-26 V: a buck alone drops out near the 21 V stop under load; 3.4 A peak out
converter_choice.12 V buck (arm): 12 V, 8 A, in the power stack (the riser buck is gone); 6.7 A peak out
converter_choice.5 V buck: 5 V, 5 A (25 W): 2.2 A peak out, room for a powered USB hub or a head camera later

19V.what: DC-DC 24 V to 19 V 10 A 190 W buck, IP67
19V.size_src: a comparable 24-19 V 10 A potted unit (VERIFY)
19V.issue: input floor 22 V: a 6S pack is under 22 V for its last stretch (3.67 V / cell) and sags under it in a burst well before the 21 V stop, so the computer's supply would leave its spec: bench-test the dropout at 20-22 V and 3.4 A, or use a buck-boost

12V.what: Proshopping DC-DC buck 15-90 V to 12 V 8 A 96 W, waterproof
12V.size_src: ASSUMED: the potted 8 A class (no size in the listing)

5V.what: LeMotech DC 12/24 V to 5 V 5 A 25 W, IP68
5V.size_src: ASSUMED: comparable 5 A 25 W potted units are 66 x 60 x 22-23

fuses.main (battery +, at the board input): 30 A slow (ATO / mini blade): above the 20 A burst, below the 12 AWG pigtail
fuses.motor bus (after the contactor): 20 A, or 4 x 7.5 A, one per motor XT30 (a shorted lead then stops one wheel)

computer_direct_from_battery: no: the BMAX takes 19 V (maker: 19 V / 3.42 A); the pack is 25.2 V full, 22.2 nominal, 21 V at the stop. Feed it from the 19 V buck-boost on the battery side of the e-stop (an e-stop must not reboot the computer). Only a PC rated for a wide input (e.g. 12-28 V) could take the pack directly.
notes: e-stop cuts the motor bus and the arm (contactor / anti-spark); the computer, MCU, lidar and face stay up
regen: the AK40-10s brake into the bus; with the contactor open at speed the back-EMF at the 44.9 rad/s cap is ~25 V (10:1, KV 170): a 30 V TVS on the motor bus (VERIFY)
all values est unless sourced; nothing measured
